description:
Relates to #1201 

Even if `PackageDir` relates to file paths, it uses forward slashes consistently, even on Windows. This PR addresses that by using forward slashes in `PackageDir` field and fixes related tests.

This PR fixes:

- TestCachedProviderHash
- TestInstallPackage
- TestLinkFromOtherCache

comments.body: What's with this extra string addition?
Only the last one is needed; I was testing whether I also need to add the backslash and forgot to change it back. Thanks for catching that.

Some of the Windows API functions for translating error codes into error strings return localized error messages and so results vary depending on what UI language is configured for the active user. 

Have you checked whether Go is always getting the English version, or could this potentially be different on a non-English system?

Maybe we could avoid the question by calling the `Error` method directly on the `Errno` value for this error in `x/sys/windows`; I assume that's the same thing that's happening to generate the error message we're trying to compare to.

A similar argument could apply on other supported platforms using the `Errno` type from `x/sys/unix`, because I don't think it's actually required for all Unix systems to use the same string to describe `ENOENT`, but it does at least seem like we've gotten away with assuming that both Linux and macOS are consistent here.

(Unfortunately if we start using `x/sys/windows` and `x/sys/unix` here then we will probably need to use conditional compilation instead of a runtime check of `GOOS`, to avoid trying to link that package into test programs on non-Windows systems.)

From some quick reading of the code it seems little on Unix systems Go uses a pregenerated table of errors strings per GOOS and GOARCH and then uses that to translate errno into string: https://github.com/golang/go/blob/d52a56cce1cc78eeff753d952d7abfc109f78ead/src/syscall/zerrors_linux_amd64.go#L1357

...but on Windows there is more complex handling involving a lookup cache, suggesting that it probably is making an OS API call and wants to make that call only once per error code: https://github.com/golang/go/blob/d52a56cce1cc78eeff753d952d7abfc109f78ead/src/syscall/syscall_windows.go#L142

These are actually from the `syscall` package rather than `x/sys`, which I think means we'd definitely need to use conditional compilation of we wanted to try to discover the error text automatically because the `Errno` constant to use is `ENOENT` on Unix but either `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` or `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND` on Windows. 🤔
Interesting investigation, @apparentlymart! I hadn't thought about that since we're usually using English systems, but it's probably more robust to write it like that.

The main point is: we're actually searching for the string in these error messages because it looks for specific errors like "could not read package directory: open testdata/cachedir/registry.opentofu.org/missing/packagedir/2.0.0/linux_amd64:" and "could not find executable file starting with terraform-provider-executable," so it's not just the not found error message. Let me think about what the best approach might be.

One of the errors is returned by this function here: https://github.com/opentofu/opentofu/blob/22910f2b01f7ade5aa9ec7505f9e24dfe65e5e6c/internal/providercache/cached_provider.go#L108-L155

So we need to create a custom error type to be tested by this test function: 

https://github.com/opentofu/opentofu/blob/22910f2b01f7ade5aa9ec7505f9e24dfe65e5e6c/internal/providercache/cached_provider_test.go#L87-L93
I mean, this can be done as well, but first I'm wondering if it's worth the effort and whether it should be in a separate PR if we're going to do this refactoring. What do you think?
That sounds a reasonable compromise, let me investigate if that would work. Thanks!
